segments.text: Your bedtime screen may keep you awake longer.
You get in bed. One more video, one more scroll. The screen glows, and sleep waits.
In a 2015 lab study, people who read on a glowing screen before bed took longer to fall asleep than when they read a printed book. They also felt less alert the next morning.
So try a wind-down. One: dim the lights an hour before bed. Two: swap the screen for a paper book. Three: repeat both steps in the same order every night.
segments.say: So try a wined-down. One: dim the lights an hour before bed. Two: swap the screen for a paper book. Three: repeat both steps in the same order every night.

segments.text: It was one lab study, so results vary. If you have a sleep condition, ask a clinician.
Try it today: dim your lights one hour before bed.
